_comment: SAPM Key Management Policy — defines generation, storage, rotation, distribution, revocation, and break-glass procedures for all key material.
_status: Approved for Alpha mainnet launch gate

keyGenerationPolicy.mechanism: Ed25519 ephemeral keypairs generated via @mysten/sui/keypairs/ed25519; never derived from weak entropy or static seeds in production
keyGenerationPolicy.seedEntropy: Minimum 256-bit cryptographically secure random source (crypto.randomBytes in Node.js runtime)
keyGenerationPolicy.storageTarget: Ephemeral keys held only in process memory; persistent keys use operator-provisioned KMS (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, or equivalent HSM-backed store)
keyGenerationPolicy.prohibition: No private key material may be written to disk, repository, container image, environment variable file committed to VCS, or log output
keyGenerationPolicy.ciEnforcement: scripts/scan_secrets.sh run as CI gate (secrets-scan job) on every push and PR

sessionKeys.rotationTrigger: Per-connection; a new session key is derived for every peer discovery exchange
sessionKeys.procedure: Orchestrator lifecycle controller resets provider state; new readiness check and key derivation on next exchange
sessionKeys.testEvidence: agents/orchestrator/test/security-hardening.test.js — lifecycle stop/start and key derivation regression tests

operatorSigningKeys.rotationPeriod: 90 days or immediately on compromise indication
operatorSigningKeys.procedure: 1. Generate replacement key in KMS. 2. Update registry verification key reference. 3. Run attestation validation smoke test. 4. Revoke old key in registry. 5. Confirm fail-closed behavior with stale key.
operatorSigningKeys.testEvidence: Pending: requires production KMS environment; documented procedure above is the tested runbook target

secretDistributionPolicy.mechanism: Secrets injected at runtime via KMS API calls or operator-managed secret manager (never baked into images or config files)
secretDistributionPolicy.accessControl: Least-privilege IAM roles; agent runtime reads only the specific secrets it needs
revocationProcedure: 1. Identify compromised secret and notify incident commander.
2. Immediately revoke in KMS/secret manager — this blocks any new reads.
3. Rotate dependent keys (session keys, signing keys) per rotation policy above.
4. Re-deploy affected agents with replacement secrets.
5. Confirm all service health checks pass before declaring incident closed.
secretDistributionPolicy.auditLog: All secret read and rotation events are logged in KMS audit trail with timestamp, principal, and secret identifier

breakGlassPolicy.credentials: Break-glass credentials are stored in a dedicated, isolated KMS key store accessible only to Engineering Leadership and Security Lead
breakGlassPolicy.auditRequirement: Every break-glass access event must be logged with timestamp, accessor identity, reason, and incident reference
breakGlassPolicy.inventoryReviewCadence: Quarterly — verify break-glass accounts exist, are scoped correctly, and have not been used without a corresponding incident record
breakGlassPolicy.revocationOnUse: After any break-glass use, the credential is rotated and the prior credential is revoked before incident is closed

complianceNotes: Key material stored outside this policy (e.g., locally for development) must use .gitignore exclusion and must never be committed.
This policy is reviewed at each release gate and updated after any security incident involving key material.
Production deployment requires HSM or cloud KMS backing. Software-only key stores are not approved for mainnet.
